usage: This is the most common and versatile way to say goodbye across the Levant, suitable for both formal and casual situations. Traditionally, it is said by the person staying to the person leaving, but today it is frequently used interchangeably by both parties. In casual settings, younger people often mix Arabic and English, simply saying 'yalla bye'.

variants.label: by your leave (to a man)
variants.note: Said by the person leaving to a male host or friend.

variants.label: by your leave (to a woman)
variants.note: Said by the person leaving to a female host or friend.

variants.label: God be with you (to a man)
variants.note: Said by the person staying to a man who is leaving.

variants.label: casual / modern
variants.note: Extremely common among younger people and in casual settings.

responses.english: may God keep you safe (said to a man)
God be with you (said to a man)

examples.arabic: يَلّا يا جَماعَة، أَنا رايِح، مَع السَّلامَة.
examples.transliteration: yalla ya jama3a, ana raye7, ma3 as-salameh.

examples.arabic: مَع السَّلامَة، دير بالَك عَلى حالَك.
